description: Abell 24 is a beautiful nebula that is rarely photographed due to its lack of popularity. This deep sky object is almost entirely made of Hydrogen-Alpha gas, often giving it its red color in photographs. Abell 24 looks like a rose, although it sadly does not have a common nickname.
name: Abell 24

description: "Abell 39 is a beautifully symmetrical planetary nebula resembling a delicate soap bubble that lies in the constellation Hercules. It's quite faint at magnitude 13.7, but an apparent size of 2.6' makes it a viable target if you attempt a long exposure on a moonless night from a rural location. Some 6,600 light-years from Earth, the actual diameter of the planetary is about five light-years. Abell 39's bubble is the expanded outer layers of the ancient subdwarf O-type star at its centre, glowing at magnitude 15.6."
name: Abell 39

description:
"The Hydra Cluster I, also known as Abell 1060 (ACO 1060), is a group of galaxies in the Hydra constellation. The size of the cluster is estimated at 10 million light-years and it contains at least 317 galaxies, the main ones being NGC 3309, NGC 3311, and NGC 3312. The first two are elliptical galaxies while the last one is a spiral galaxy slightly larger than the Milky Way. As is the case for all galaxies and clusters of galaxies, the structure is surrounded by a gigantic halo of dark matter.

So, on the image, the many bright points are not stars but galaxies located more than 150 million light-years away from us."
name: Hydra Cluster I

description: "Abell 3526 is the name given to a galaxy cluster containing more than 100 members in the southern constellation Centaurus (The Centaur), located about 170 million light-years from Earth. Commonly known as the Centaurus Cluster, Abell 3526 spans six degrees of sky, so you must use Singularity's mosaic mode to capture it. The cluster's brightest member is NGC 4696, a magnitude 11.4 elliptical galaxy with an apparent size of 4' x 3' that lies about 120 million light-years from us. Several dwarf elliptical galaxies surround it."
name: Centaurus Cluster

description: Beta Cygni, known as Albireo, is a double star system in the constellation Cygnus. Albireo can be seen using binoculars or any size telescopes. This is an excellent target for photography because of the color difference between the two stars. The brightest member, Albireo A, shines yellow at magnitude 3.1, whereas the smaller star, Albireo B, has a very strong blue hue and has a magnitude of 5.1).
name: Albireo

description:
"Aldebaran, also known as Alpha Tauri, is the brightest star in the Taurus constellation. It is an evolved giant orange star. Indeed, it has exhausted the hydrogen supply in its core and it is now burning its helium. With a mass 1.13 times that of the Sun, it is very similar to our star. At a more advanced stage in its life cycle, however, it is 500 times brighter. Being a giant star, it is 45 times larger than the Sun and its surface temperature is about 1,500°C cooler, but twice that needed to melt iron.
Although Aldebaran is close to the Hyades cluster in the sky, it does not belong to it. With an estimated distance of 66 light-years, it is 90 light-years closer to us than the open cluster is."
name: Alpha Tauri

description:
"Gamma Leonis is a binary star system that is part of a 6-star asterism known as the Sickle, in the constellation of Leo. Both stars can be independently observed with a regular amateur telescope and display an interesting difference in apparent colors: the brightest of the two, Gamma Leo A, shines with orange whereas the second one, Gamma Leonis B features a greenish yellow tint. This slight tint difference reflects different surface temperatures between the two.
One orbiting around the other at a distance equivalent to 4 times the Sun-to-Pluto distances, one would need to wait 510 years for the Gamma Leonis system to complete a full revolution!"
name: Gamma Leonis

description:
"Alpha Centauri is the brightest star system in the Centaurus constellation. It is actually a triple-star system! Alpha Centauri A and Alpha Centauri B form the main pair accompanied by a third star, Alpha Centauri C. The latter, also known as Proxima Centauri, is the closest star to the Sun.

The two main stars orbit each other in 79.91 years and their distance varies between 11.2 and 35.6 astronomical units, that is, between the orbit of Saturn and that of Pluto. The third star, on the other hand, needs 547,000 years to complete a single orbit.

The total weight of the three stars is a little more than twice the mass of the Sun."
name: Alpha Centauri

description: "Alshain is the proper name of Beta Aquilae, the naked-eye star that, for Northern Hemisphere observers, lies a little more than the width of a thumb at arm's length to the lower-left of Altair, the brightest in the constellation Aquila (The Eagle). Despite its Bayer classification of Beta, magnitude 3.7 Alshain is the seventh-brightest star in Aquila. Although it has a similar G-class spectrum to our Sun, Alshain is about six times brighter and is poised to become a red giant star. Alshain is almost 45 light-years from Earth."
name: Alshain

description: Antares is a binary star system in the Scorpius constellation. The primary star (the most massive in the system) Antares A, also known as Alpha Scorpii A, is a red supergiant star like Betelgeuse, which is in the Orion constellation. Distinctly red in the sky, it is 62,500 times more luminous than the Sun. A significant portion of the light it emits is in the infrared band, which is not visible to the human eye. Its surface temperature is about 3,000°C, which is a little more than half that of the Sun. The star has a mass equivalent to 18 times that of the Sun for a diameter 680 times bigger. So, if we replaced the Sun in our system by this supergiant, its surface would exceed the orbit of Mars. During this phase of its lifespan, Antares ejects the equivalent of 6 Mars’ per year into the interstellar medium. This matter forms a shell of gas and dust around the star. At only 15 million years old, the star is already at the end of its lifespan. It should explode into a supernova “soon” (soon in terms of a star’s lifespan). When this happens, it will be as bright as a full Moon for a few weeks.
name: Antares

description: "Arcturus (guardian of the bear in Greek), Hokule'a (star of gladness in Hawaiian), or Da Jiao (great horn in Chinese), is the brightest star in the Boötes constellation. It is a red giant like what the Sun will become in a few billion years. It is 25 times bigger than our Sun and 170 times brighter. A large portion of the light it emits is infrared, invisible to the human eye. Because it grew, its surface temperature lowered, and with its 4,000 degrees, it is 1,500°C cooler than the Sun. It is also 5% more massive than our Sun, and with its 7 billion years, a little older too. In a few billion years, it will become a planetary nebula."
name: Arcturus

description: "Barnard's Star is a star in the Ophiuchus constellation. It is a red dwarf star with a very low mass of barely 20% that of the Sun. It is barely twice as massive as the minimum required to become a star. The star is also 5,000 times less luminous than the Sun and its surface temperature is about 3,000 degrees. With this characteristic, the star mainly emits red light. Until 1998, it was believed that the star, at one billion years old, was now quiet and that the regular eruptions and violent storms of its youth were no longer happening. A violent eruption was however observed on July 17, 1998; it tore matter from the star and heated it to more than 8,000 degrees."
name: "Barnard's Star"

description: "Barnard 72, better known as the Snake, is a dark nebula appearing to slither across the rich Milky Way star fields of the constellation Ophiuchus (The Serpent Handler). Unlike emission nebulae that glow, dark nebulae are opaque clouds of gas and dust seen as silhouettes against background objects. Named after pioneering astrophotographer Edward Emerson Barnard who published a catalog of 182 'dark markings on the sky' in 1919, S-shaped Barnard 72 is one of the most impenetrable examples, rating 6 on the six-point Lynds opacity scale. It lies 650 light-years from Earth and appears as large as the full Moon."
name: Snake Nebula

description: "Not all deep-sky objects glow against the night's velvet backdrop. Some, like Barnard 84 (LDN 235) here, are dense interstellar clouds known as dark nebulae that obscure the visible wavelengths of light from more distant objects and appear silhouetted against them. Barnard 84 lies in the southern constellation Sagittarius (The Archer) and is named after American astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard, a pioneering celestial photographer and an observer with exceptional eyesight. He published a catalog of dark nebulae compiled from his photographs in 1919. From its shape, Barnard 84 is commonly called The Claw Nebula or The Dark Scorpion."
name: Barnard 84

description: "Barnard 150, popularly known as the Seahorse, is a dark nebula in the Northern Hemisphere constellation Cepheus (The King). Once believed to be holes or voids in the Milky Way, dark nebulae are opaque clouds of gas and dust obscuring the light from more distant stars. The Seahorse Nebula is particularly dark, rating 5 out of 6 on the Lynds opacity scale. It lies about 1,200 light-years from Earth, where its apparent size of 75' suggests an actual width of 26 light-years. The Fireworks Galaxy (NGC 6946) lies four Moon-widths west of Barnard 150, so try using Singularity's mosaic mode to capture both in the same field of view."
name: Seahorse Nebula

description: Barnard 174, or LDN 1164, is a dark nebula in the Northern Hemisphere constellation Cepheus (The King). It lies two Moon widths to the upper-right of third-magnitude star Zeta Cephei. Appearing as an irregularly shaped silhouette in the Milky Way about half the size of a full Moon, Barnard 174 is an opaque cloud of gas and dust obscuring the light of star-rich regions beyond — and it is dark, rating 6 on the six-point Lynds opacity scale. Telescopes sensitive to infrared light show that the nebula is an active star-forming region populated with clusters of young suns.
name: Barnard 174

description: "Barnard 252, commonly known as the Dolphin, is a dark nebula swimming through the rich star fields of the constellation Scorpius (The Scorpion). This dolphin appears in silhouette because it comprises a cloud of obscuring gas and dust hiding the stars beyond. Named after pioneering astrophotographer Edward Emerson Barnard who published a catalogue of 'dark markings on the sky', Barnard 252 is particularly impenetrable, rating 5 on the six-point Lynds opacity scale. It appears two-thirds the width of a full Moon."
name: Dolphin Nebula

description: Beta Cephei is a triple star system within the Cepheus constellation. It is formed by two gravity-bound stars and another star in the line of sight that does not interact with the first two. The main star of the binary system is Alfirk: a giant blue star, 23,000 times brighter than our Sun and featuring a surface temperature of 26,000 degrees Kelvin! The companion star orbiting around Alfirk, Beta Cephei Ab, is so close that it remains difficult and nearly impossible to detect with telescopes - even professional ones. The third star, Beta Cephei B is far enough to be detected with a small diameter commercial telescope.
name: Beta Cephei

description:
"Betelgeuse is one of the 10 brightest stars in our sky, the 9th more precisely. It is part of the winter star Orion constellation. It is not the brightest of the constellation as that role is filled by the blue supergiant Rigel.
Located on Orion's left shoulder and easily recognizable thanks to its orange color, this red supergiant at the end of its life (approximately 10 million years old) is 1,000 times bigger than the Sun and brighter than 100,000 Suns combined."
name: Betelgeuse

description: The comet C/2019 Y4 was discovered by the ATLAS (Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System) automated survey program on December 28, 2019. It should become visible to the naked eye in the beginning of May 2020.
name: C/2019 Y4 (ATLAS)

description:
"Canopus, also known as Alpha Carinae, is the brightest star in the constellation Carina. It is also the 2nd brightest star in the sky after Sirius. The star is classified as a yellow supergiant. It is therefore very large and very extensive. Its radius is estimated at 70 times that of the Sun. It shines like 18,000 Suns and weighs about 10 solar masses. Its age is estimated at 30 million years. This massive star has exhausted its reserves of hydrogen in its core and now uses helium to create its light.
Several studies have shown the presence of spots on the surface of the star as for the Sun with sunspots. However, the precision of instruments and measurements to date do not allow us to study these in detail."
name: Alpha Carinae

description:
"Capella, also known as Alpha Aurigae, is the brightest star in the Auriga constellation. Although it appears to be a single star to the naked eye, it is actually a double binary system. The first binary system consists of 2 giant stars that are separated by 0.74 astronomical units (AU) and orbit each other every 104 days. Each of the two stars is 2.5 times as massive as the Sun, 70 times brighter, and has a surface temperature between 5000 and 5700°C.
Located 10,000 AU away, the second pair consists of two red dwarfs that are separated by 40 AU and orbit each other every 300 years. This pair weighs about half the mass of the Sun."
name: Alpha Aurigae

description: Collinder 261 is an open cluster in the Musca constellation. According to the most recent data from the Gaia Mission, the cluster contains more than 1,800 members. Within this population, there are 54 blue straggler stars. These stars are brighter and more massive than the rest of the population. They also appear bluer than the rest of the stars. At almost seven billion years old, it is one of the oldest open clusters in the Milky Way. The stars formed in a molecular cloud the chemical composition of which was close to that of our Sun.
name: Collinder 261

description: The Hanger Cluster, also known as the Brocchi Cluster or Collinder 399, is an asterism located in the constellation of Vulpecula. Its first description was made by the persian astronomer Al Sufi in his catalog “The Book of Fixed Stars” in 964. For many years, stars were thought to be members of a young star cluster. However, the distance measurements of the stars in 1998 by the Hipparcos satellite demonstrate that the stars did not form a cluster and that they were just a beautiful alignment in the sky. Thus the brightest stars of the cluster are located between 200 and 1200 light-years.
name: "Brocchi's Cluster"

description: Delta Cephei is beyond the shadow of a doubt the most famous variable star since it served as a model for establishing the Cepheids class of variable stars. Delta Cephei was discovered in 1784 by the 20-year-old English astronomer John Goodricke who measured a luminosity varying from 3.5th to 4.4th magnitude within a period of 5.36 days. At the time, one thought the variable property was caused by another star partially eclipsing Delta Cephei. Today, we know this occurs due to repetitive contraction and expansion processes taking place at the surface level. Thus, the brightness of the star is lower when its surface expands under the high-pressure of thermonuclear reactions and the star’s brightness is higher when the cooled gas steps back to the surface due to gravity.
name: Delta Cephei

description: Deneb is the brightest star in the Cygnus constellation. It is a white supergiant star 200 times bigger than the Sun. If we were to replace the Sun by this star, its surface would be about ten million or so kilometers from Earth. It is also 60,000 times brighter than the Sun and has a surface temperature 3,000 degrees hotter. At about ten million years old, Deneb has finished burning the hydrogen in its core, it is now composed of Helium. The latter is starting to transform into carbon. With a mass at origin 20 times that of the Sun, the star should become a red supergiant like Betelgeuse in a few million years before dying in a supernova explosion, when its core will have turned into iron.
name: Alpha Cygni

description: "The Triple Cave Nebula is a dark nebula in the Aquila constellation. It consists of the nebulae Barnard 142 and Barnard 143. In the middle of a field of stars, there is a large black area that forms the letter E in the sky. Because of its distinctive shape, it is sometimes called Barnard's E Nebula. This region is composed of several small molecular clouds of very cold and not very dense gas. The total mass of the structure is estimated to be 430 times the mass of the Sun distributed across a ring that is about 2 light-years in diameter. No star formation has been detected in this cloud."
name: Triple Cave Nebula

description: Epsilon Lyrae is not only defined as being the fifth brightest star in the Lyra constellation. It actually contains a 4-star system, all linked by gravity, hence its “Double Double” nickname. With binoculars, Epsilon Lyrae splits into two main stars 0.16 light-years apart. With a telescope powerful enough, both of them split into two as well. This multiple star system is located 162 light-years away from Earth, almost 7 times farther than the main star of the constellation Lyra, Vega. In 1985, a fifth star belonging to the Epsilon Lyrae system was discovered by an interferometric method.
name: Double Double star

description: Eta Cassiopeiae is a binary star neighboring the Earth, about 20 light-years away from the Cassiopeia constellation. Its main feature is in the color contrast of its primary and secondary stars. The first one, Eta Cassiopeiae A, is a shiny yellowish-white dwarf star whereas the second one, Eta Cassiopeiae B, is an orange dwarf with a luminosity 30 times fainter. Although Cassiopeia is one of the simplest constellations to identify in the night sky, Eta Cassiopeia remains, however, barely visible to the naked eye and requires the use of a telescope to distinguish both stars that are 71 astronomical units apart. Such a small angular separation between the two stars as seen from the Earth is tantamount to observing an Airbus A320 from a distance equal to that of Boston-Washington!
name: Eta Cassiopeiae

description: Gamma Librae is a yellow giant star in the constellation Libra. It is the sixth brightest star used to identify the constellation. It is also known as Zubenelhakrabi, which means “the claws of the scorpion”. This name was given when the constellation Scorpius was larger and before the constellation Libra was created. The star weighs 1.5 times the mass of our Sun, it is 11 times larger, and 1.5 billion years younger. With a surface temperature of 4,500°C, it is 950°C cooler than the Sun. It is however still hot enough to melt all our metals. The star has consumed the hydrogen in its core and is starting to burn the hydrogen in its outer parts, causing it to expand. One study suggests the star is actually a binary system.
name: Zubenelhakrabi

description: "The Grus Quartet is the popular name of an attractive gathering of four gravitationally-bound spiral galaxies — NGC 7552, 7582, 7590 and NGC 7599 — in the southern constellation Grus (The Crane). Scottish astronomer James Dunlop discovered them from Australia in 1826. NGC 7582 is the largest (5') and brightest (magnitude 10.6) of the four and contains a supermassive black hole. The galaxy shows high levels of starburst activity, as does NGC 7552, due to the gravitational forces between them. The Grus Quartet lies about 65 million light-years from Earth."
name: Grus Quartet

description: GUM 39, also referenced as IC 2872, is an emission nebula located in the Centaurus constellation. This nebula forms the Head of the Running Chicken Nebula (IC 2944) located next to it. The image also contains a second emission nebula, GUM 40. They are part of the same molecular cloud in which a new generation of stars is forming. These reservoirs of matter owe their illumination and their red color to gas heated by the massive stars HD 99897 and HD 99898 respectively.
name: GUM 39

description: CPD-54 6791, also known as GUM 49 or the Coffee Bean Nebula, is a multiple star close to a gas cloud located in the Norma constellation. The molecular cloud of a few hundred solar masses is divided into two bright regions. The edge of the cloud has been glowing red for 100,000 years when light and matter ejected from CPD-54,6791 began to impact the gas cloud and heat it. In the heart of the cloud, new stars are forming and should eventually tear the cloud apart to reveal a new open star cluster.
name: CPD-54 6791

description: The Broken Engagement Ring is an asterism that lies close to the star Merak in the Ursa Major constellation. A dozen or so stars form the letter C in the sky giving the impression of a broken ring.
name: Broken Engagement Ring

description: "IC 1318, commonly known as the Butterfly Nebula, is an extensive emission nebula in the northern constellation Cygnus (The Swan). It lies closely east of second-magnitude foreground star Sadr (Gamma Cygni), near the centre of the constellation's prominent cross-shaped asterism. The wings of this celestial papillon extend on either side of the dark nebula LDN 889. The Butterfly Nebula lies about 4,900 light-years from Earth, where its apparent width of almost three times that of the full Moon corresponds to an actual size of 120 light-years."
name: Butterfly Nebula

description: IC 1396 is a large emission nebula in the constellation Cepheus. It is located about 3,000 light-years away from Earth. The gases in IC 1396 are visible thanks to the very bright blue star that shines in its center.
name: "Elephant's Trunk Nebula"

description: IC 1795 is an emission nebula spanning over 70 light-years in diameter. It is located 6,000 light-years away in the constellation Cassiopeia. IC 1795 is mostly known as the Fishhead Nebula due to its shape when photographed.
name: Fishhead Nebula

description: IC 1805 is an emission nebula spanning about 200 light-years in the constellation Cassiopeia. Also known as the Heart Nebula, it presents glowing ionized hydrogen gas and darker dust clouds which give it its heart-shape. In its center, we can find the young cluster Melotte 15 (1.5 million years old), home of a few bright stars nearly 50 times the mass of our Sun.
name: Heart Nebula

description: IC 1848 is an emission nebula spanning about 100 light-years in the constellation Cassiopeia. Also known as the Soul Nebula, it is home to several open clusters of stars and huge evacuated bubbles formed by the winds of young massive stars. Its red tint is due to the emission of hydrogen gas.
name: Soul Nebula

description: Spreading over 100 light-years, the Seagull Nebula is an emission nebula located about 3,800 light-years away from Earth. It is located right on the edge between the constellation Monoceros and Canis Major. In this region of the Milky Way, one can also distinguish other deep-sky objects such as the open clusters NGC 2335, NGC 2343, NGC 2353 and, further north, Messier 50.
name: Seagull Nebula

description:
"Located 500 light-years away, IC 2391 is an open star cluster in the Vela constellation. It is made up of a total of 39 stars, 8 of which can be seen by the naked eye.
IC 2391 might look like a trivial object, but is actually of great scientific interest. On top of being a cluster of gravitationally unbound stars (the proper definition of an open cluster), IC 2391 is a moving stellar group: stars all move in similar fashion. This property allows astronomers to accurately study the trajectory of stars in close proximity to our solar system."
name: IC 2391

description:
"IC 2602 is the third most luminous open star cluster in the sky. Located in the Carina constellation and near the unmissable Carina nebula, IC 2602’s significant blue color and great brightness gave it a second name : the Southern Pleiades. This refers to an obvious deep sky object: the Pleiades open star cluster M45 in the Northern hemisphere or the sky’s second brightest cluster. 
 
IC 2602 counts approximately 60 stars with less than a dozen spottable by the naked eye. 
 
It mainly consists of hot and massive stars as young as 30 to 46 million years, which is still between 100 to 150 times younger than our Sun."
name: Southern Pleiades

description: IC 2714 is an open cluster in the constellation Carina. It was discovered by James Dunlop in 1826. It is located approximately 4,000 light years away from Earth, in the Carina–Sagittarius Arm.
name: Melotte 104

description:
"IC2 944 is a nebula located near the bright star Lambda Centauri (magnitude 3.1). It is sometimes called Lambda Centauri Nebula but more commonly Running Chicken Nebula.
It is home to, and is associated with, an open cluster of young stars a few million years old (by comparison our Sun is 4.5 billion years old). The intense ultraviolet radiation from these stars is the main energy source that illuminates the hydrogen clouds of the nebula."
name: Running Chicken Nebula

description: IC 342, also known as Caldwell 5, is a spiral galaxy in the Giraffe Constellation. It appears dim and reddened as it lies close to the galactic plane, while the light it emits must pass through the gas and dust clouds of the Milky Way before it reaches Earth. As the galaxy is relatively close to us in the universe, IC 342 was initially thought to be part of the same group of galaxies as the Milky Way. However, research has shown that IC 342 actually belongs to a group of galaxies close to ours, called IC 342/Maffei14.
name: IC 342

description: IC 405, also known as the Flaming Star Nebula, is an emission and reflection nebula located in the constellation Auriga. It surrounds the bluish star AE Aurigae and shines at magnitude 6.
name: Flaming Star Nebula

description:
"IC 410, also known as The Tadpoles Nebula, is an emission nebula in the Auriga constellation. The nebula shelters the open star cluster NGC 1893 in its center.
The mass of the cluster is estimated to be more than 1,300 solar masses, one-third of which corresponds to the mass of its 35 most massive stars. The first stars in the cluster formed 1.5 million years ago and there are currently more than 200 protostars in a cube 3 light-years across. The young stars in the cluster heat and sculpt the gas of the nebula, which mainly consists of hydrogen that will emit red light.
The nebula’s reservoir of gas is still rich and dense. A study based on X-ray light suggests there could be more than 4,600 nearly formed stars still hidden in the depths of the nebula."
name: Tadpoles Nebula

description: IC 417, also known as SH 2-234, is an emission nebula in the Auriga constellation. Buried in its core is the open cluster Stock 8. It contains at least 348 young stars and a great many stars in formation. These young stellar objects are less than 5 million years old. In the molecular cloud containing the nebula and the cluster, 2 matter condensation regions have been observed. At 25 to 30 light-years in length, the first region weighs more than 1,000 solar masses. The 2nd, similar in size, only weighs 400 solar masses.
name: Spider Nebula

description: The Horsehead Nebula is located in the Orion constellation, near the star Zeta Orionis, or Alnitak, found at the end of the Orion Belt. This dark nebula can be found in a region poor of stars which concentrate dense clouds of dust blocking the light emitted by the stars behind. The Horsehead is an object very much appreciated by observers, it is visible in winter in the Northern Hemisphere, and in summer in the Southern Hemisphere.
name: Horsehead Nebula

description: "IC443, also known as the Jellyfish Nebula, is a supernova remnant found in the Gemini constellation, near the Eta Geminorum or Propus star. This gas cloud is the residue of a star explosion that dates back to an uncertain time (between 3000 and 30,000 years). The nebula presents two asymmetrical lobes, weakly connected to each other, the most luminous and compact lobe forming the jellyfish's umbrella."
name: Jellyfish Nebula

description: "The Blue Horsehead nebula, formally IC 4592, is a reflection nebula in the constellation Scorpius (The Scorpion) 400 light-years away. In common with other reflection nebulae, IC 4592's characteristic colour is caused by the scattering of blue light by interstellar dust. The source of illumination in this instance is the star Nu Scorpii, commonly known as Jabbah, which forms the horse's eye. The Blue Horsehead Nebula is faint and extensive, so you will need a dark, moonless, rural sky and a long exposure in Mosaic Mode to capture it."
name: Blue Horsehead nebula

description: Located in the south of the constellation Scorpius, IC4628 nicknamed Shrimp Nebula is an emission nebula whose size is more than 200 light-years (8 times bigger than the Orion nebula). In our sky, its apparent size is about 3 times the size of the full Moon.
name: Prawn Nebula

description: "IC 4651 is a bright magnitude 6.9 open star cluster in the southern constellation Ara (The Altar). It lies 1.1 degrees east of magnitude 2.8 naked-eye star Alpha Arae, so you can capture both in the same field of view using Singularity's Mosaic Mode. Scottish astronomer James Dunlop discovered IC 4651 in 1826. The cluster appears 10' in size, suggesting an actual diameter of about 8½ light-years at a distance of 2,900 light-years from Earth."
name: IC 4651

description: IC 4665, also known as the Summer Beehive Cluster, is an open cluster in the constellation Ophiuchus. There are currently 800 stars in this young cluster. Which is slightly more than the number of people who have been to space. Its stars formed less than 30 million years ago.  The most brilliant blue stars are massive, hot, and very bright. Their surface temperatures can reach 15,000°C and they shine like 900 Suns.
name: Summer Beehive Cluster

description:
"IC 4685 is a beautiful emission nebula that is situated in the middle of a complex region filled with emission and reflection nebulae found in the Sagittarius constellation.
Since it is near the celestial equator it can be viewed by observers located in both Northern and Southern Hemisphere. Sitting about 4000 light years from Earth, this dense star cloud exhibits an intricate structure and luminosity that appears about as large as the disk of our Moon.
IC4685 has a winding river of dark filaments flowing through the nebula and displays vibrant shades of ionized hydrogen gas in striking red hues, leaving observers mesmerized."
name: IC 4685

description: IC 4756, also known as Graff’s Cluster, is an open cluster in the Serpens Constellation. The stars in the cluster are about 890 million years old. From our position, the dust is not uniformly distributed over the cluster, which can lead to slight variations in color. 644 stars have been listed as members of the cluster, including a dozen evolved giant stars.
name: "Graff's Cluster"

description: IC 5070 is an emission nebula, in the Cygnus the Swan constellation, where star formation is particularly active. The nebula is located near the magnitude 1 star Deneb, one of the 3 stars of the Summer Triangle, and next to the North America nebula (NGC 7000); they are separated by a dark cloud of obscuring dust.
name: Pelican Nebula

description: In reality, IC 5146 represents two distinct objects: the emission nebula known as the Cocoon, and the open cluster known as Collinder 470. Located approximately 4000 light-years from Earth in the Cygnus constellation, it is a region where there is much star formation activity, this region is designated as filled with star nurseries.
name: Cocoon Nebula

description: IC 59 is very close to IC 63 and the two are almost always photographed as a pair. IC 59 is a reflection nebula whereas IC 63 is a mix of emission and reflection nebula. The two are very faint and difficult to spot as they are close to the bright star Gamma Cassiopeia.
name: Ghost of Cassiopeia

description:
"Iota Orionis is a multiple star system lying in the same field of view as the so-called great Orion nebula.
Its main star, named Hatsya, is remarkable: not only in that it is the brightest star of Orion’s sword but it is also a heartbeat star. Hatsya is indeed influenced by a close hot companion that completes a full orbit in 29 days, and is located half as close as the Earth -Sun’s distance! Imagine two stars that are just half an astronomical unit apart: this is the case of Iota Orionis. The elliptical trajectory of the companion star triggers a strong tidal force on both of them that deforms their geometry. Such surface perturbation can be detected from Earth as it also influences the intensity of light relative to time: the light curve of Iota Orionis follows a periodic signal similar to a heartbeat, hence this peculiar expression!
Thus, every 29 days, the main star of Iota Orionis undergoes tidal forces that make its overall brightness change as though a heartbeat signal, with a maximum amplitude of just 1% of its usual light intensity."
name: Iota Orionis

description: Jupiter is a huge gas planet, and is the 5th one from the Sun. One day on Jupiter is called a Jovian day, the planet rotates pretty fast, as a Jovian day resolves into just 10 Earth hours. Jupiter is very famous for its Great Red Spot, which is an enormous storm where 2 Earths could fit in. The 1979 mission to Jupiter discovered that the planet had rings, just like the other gas giants in our solar system.
name: Jupiter

description: LDN 1235, popularly known as the Dark Shark due to its shape, is an opaque nebula prowling the northern constellation Cepheus (The King). Unlike emission nebulae that glow a characteristically pink or red colour, dark nebulae are dense clouds of dust and gas obscuring the light from more distant objects — in this instance, the rich star fields of the Milky Way. The full extent of the Dark Shark Nebula is four times the width of the Moon, but its darkest portion is less than a lunar diameter wide beside the sixth-magnitude star HD 211300. Astronomers believe that LDN 1235 is about 650 light-years from Earth.
name: Dark Shark nebula

description: The Large Magellanic Cloud is a satellite galaxy of our Milky Way, and is, after the Sagittarius dwarf and the Canis Major dwarf, the third closest galaxy to us. Magellan took notes of the galaxy during his travels in 1519, and it now has his name, along with the Small Magellanic Cloud. The Large Magellanic Cloud is home to many clusters and nebulae, including the famous Tarantula Nebula!
name: Large Magellanic Cloud

description:
"The Crab Nebula, also known as M1, is a supernova remnant in the Taurus constellation. In 1054, a star exploded and was spotted in the sky by Chinese and Japanese astronomers. In 1731, nearly 700 years later, astronomer John Bevis discovered a nebula in this region. It wasn’t until the 20th century however that the nebula was determined to be a supernova remnant with a pulsar, corpse of the massive exploded star, embedded in its center.
The nebula, which is expanding at 1,500 km/s, exhibits a diversity of colors. This mosaic of colors comes from different atomic elements that shine in different colors. The orange regions consist of hydrogen. Oxygen shines blue in the outer parts. The hotter inner parts emit red light, and the green is sulfur. These colors are the result of the pulsar, approximately 20 km in diameter and 200,000 times brighter than the Sun, heating the remnant."
name: Crab Nebula

description: M10 is a globular cluster of more than 100,000 stars in the constellation of Ophiuchus. It is located 16,000 light-years from the galactic center and 14,000 light-years away from our solar system. It is often associated with M12, another globular cluster very close in distance (2000 AL) and in size, also located in the center of the constellation of Ophiuchus.
name: M10

description: Messier 100 is a grand design spiral, starburst galaxy, that is seen almost face-on. It is one of the largest and brightest galaxies of the Virgo cluster. As M100 is moving through the Virgo cluster, it is slowly losing some of its gas.
name: M100

description: M101 is a large spiral galaxy that is seen head-on. While difficult to observe due to its low surface brightness, it is an easy target for astrophotographers. Messier 101 has an asymmetrical shape, and several small galaxies surrounding the Pinwheel galaxy are to blame for pulling this beautiful Messier object with their gravitational pull.
name: Pinwheel Galaxy

description: M103 is a loose and not-so-impressive open star cluster in Cassiopeia. M103 is home to at least 172 stars, but only 4 are bright enough to be seen with binoculars, and a few others can be seen through bigger instruments and photography.
name: M103

description: Messier 104 appears as a very small object, but it holds the biggest supermassive black hole ever recorded in any nearby galaxy. Despite its small size, it is a popular target among amateur astrophotographers because of its beautiful dust lanes that cross in front of its luminous center.
name: Sombrero Galaxy

description: M105 is an elliptical galaxy in the Leo constellation. It is impossible to see any details in the galaxy with any type of instrument, so this is not a very impressive galaxy to observe or even photograph.
name: M105

description: Considered as being between a normal and a barred spiral galaxy, the 106th object on the Messier catalog has a very unique shape which makes it one of the most beautiful galaxies out there. It also has a small companion galaxy, NGC 4217, which can be seen from its edge.
name: M106

description: Messier 107 is a very loose globular cluster that is home to about 100,000 stars. It has an estimated age of 13.95 billion years, making it one of the oldest globular clusters known.
name: M107

description: In the same field of view as M97, the Owl nebula, lies a barred spiral galaxy that is popular amongst amateur observers and astrophotographers. The Surfboard galaxy, from our point of view, has a similar appearance as the Cigar galaxy (M82) although M108 does not have red gases expelling from its core.
name: Surfboard Galaxy

description: Messier 109 is a barred spiral galaxy in Ursa Major. M109 is part of the M109 group of galaxies, which contains 79 members. Messier 109 is the brightest object in the group.
name: M109

description:
"M11, the Wild Duck cluster, got its name due to the brightest stars in the cluster forming a triangle that resembles a flock of ducks flying.
It is one of the most compact and star-rich clusters out there, with about 2,900 stars!"
name: Wild Duck Cluster

description: Visible when observing or photographing the huge Andromeda galaxy (M31), M110 is one of the two dwarf elliptical galaxies that can be seen from Earth with amateur equipment.
name: Edward Young Star

description: "M12 is a globular cluster located about 15,700 light-years away from Earth. In 2006, scientists came up with the conclusion that many of M12's stars were lost because of the gravitational pull of the Milky Way galaxy. Those stars ended up drifting in our galaxy's halo."
name: M12

description: The Hercules cluster is one of the most imposing star clusters in the Messier catalog. It is made up of about as many stars as the community of Washington DC has inhabitants, more than 500,000! It is also one of the oldest observable objects in the sky.
name: Hercules Cluster

description: M14 is a globular cluster that lies about 30,300 light-years away from Earth. Charles Messier discovered this cluster in 1764 but described it as a nebula without any stars. It actually contains about 150,000 stars and its total luminosity is 400,000 times that of our Sun.
name: M14

description: M15, also called the Great Pegasus cluster, is a beautiful cluster of stars in the constellation of the Flying Horse. Although M15 is rather large, spanning over 200 light-years in diameter, its core is very small, at only 1.4 light years altogether!
name: Great Pegasus Cluster

description: M16 is a fairly large nebula in the constellation of Serpens. The Eagle nebula is one of the most well-known nebulae in the night sky, especially since the Hubble Space Telescope photographed its Pillars of Creation, in 1995.
name: Eagle Nebula

description:
"M17 is a bright diffuse emission nebula, and is also commonly named the Omega nebula or Swan nebula.
Messier 17 is very similar to M42, the famous Orion nebula, but is seen from its edge, rather than face-on like Messier 42. M17 is also about three to four times farther from Earth than the Orion nebula."
name: Omega Nebula

description: M18 is a young open cluster in the constellation of Sagittarius. It is rather difficult to spot in the night sky due to its size and the fact that it is located behind the galactic plane. Also, most of its stars are small and overall, this is a pretty faint cluster.
name: M18

description: M19 is a globular cluster with a slightly elongated shape, located near the brightest star in the constellation of the Scorpion: Antares. Messier 19 lies not far from the galactic center, at just 6,500 light-years away from the core.
name: M19

description: M2 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Aquarius, north of the star Beta Aquarii (or Sadalsuud), the brightest star in the constellation. The cluster orbits inside the halo of our galaxy, the Milky Way, and concentrates more than 150,000 stars, making it one of the largest and densest known globular clusters. Its age is estimated at 13 billion years.
name: M2

description: M20 is a nice combination of an open cluster of stars, an emission nebula (the red blob), a reflection nebula (the blue part) and a dark nebula (Barnard 85, the dark dust clouds that seem to divide the two blobs).
name: Trifid Nebula

description: M21 is a young open star cluster of about 57 stars that can be seen just next to Messier 20.
name: M21

description: At a distance of only 10,600 light-years away from Earth, M22 is, after M4, the closest Messier globular cluster to us! It is also the brightest globular cluster visible in the Northern sky, but does not rise very high above the horizon.
name: M22

description: Messier 23 is a bright and very old open cluster in the constellation of Sagittarius, not far from M20 and other great nebulae.
name: M23

description: M24 is a huge star cloud in the Sagittarius arm of the Milky Way. It contains thousands of stars, but also star clusters. Messier 24 is the densest concentration of stars visible in binoculars, with more than 1,000 stars in one field of view.
name: Sagittarius Star Cloud

description: Just West of the Sagittarius star cloud is a dim open cluster. Messier 25 is thought to contain at least 601 members, including 2 giant stars.
name: M25

description: With its brightest star being a magnitude of 11.9, M26 is another pretty faint open cluster. It is best to observe this cluster between June and September.
name: M26

description: "M27 was the first planetary object discovered by Charles Messier, in 1764. In photos, the Dumbbell nebula's inner gases have the shape of… a dumbbell! Like most other planetary nebulae, M27 is very similar to what our sun will become when it dies."
name: Dumbbell Nebula

description: M28 is a globular cluster in the constellation of Sagittarius, it has a mass of more than 550,000 solar masses and contains 50,000 confirmed stars.
name: M28

description: A very small open cluster, M29, lies at the intersection of the Northern Cross asterism, which forms the brightest stars of the constellation of the Swan: Cygnus. Messier 29 does not have a noticeable center, and it is overall a dim object.
name: M29

description: M3 is a globular cluster belonging to the constellation Canes Venatici (The Hunting Dogs), located between the star Arcturus and Cor Caroli. The cluster concentrates more than 500,000 stars and is known to host the largest number of variable stars ever observed in a globular cluster.
name: M3

description: Messier 30 is another one of those elongated looking clusters, which is not very common, especially in the Messier Catalog. M30 is about 12.93 billion years old and is approaching us at a speed of 181.9 km/s.
name: M30

description: "The Andromeda Galaxy is one of the few galaxies visible to the naked eye from Earth in the Northern hemisphere. It is also one of the biggest objects in the night sky! It is by far the most popular galaxy to capture for amateur astrophotographers, as it is the most impressive looking one. When observing or photographing M31, also look for its satellite galaxy M110, which should be obvious to notice! You might also be able to spot M32, although it may seem washed out behind M31's outer gases."
name: Andromeda Galaxy

description: Visible when observing M31, M32 is a dwarf elliptical galaxy orbiting the huge Andromeda galaxy. It is one of the two brightest satellite galaxies (with M110) that can be seen around M31. It is however too small to reveal any detail within the gases (6,500 LY vs 160,000 LY for M31). It was named after its discoverer: Guillaume Le Gentil.
name: Le Gentil

description: M33 is the second apparent largest, and brightest galaxy to observe and photograph in the night sky. It is also one of the most distant naked eye objects, as you can see M33 without any instrument, if under very clear and non-polluted dark skies.
name: Triangulum Galaxy

description: Messier 34 is a young open cluster located 1,500 light-years away from Earth, making it one of the nearest clusters from us. It is visible in the constellation of Perseus.
name: M34

description: M35 is a large, 110 million year old cluster located 2,800 light-years away in Gemini. Another cluster, NGC 2158, is visible just next to Messier 35, and the both of them together make for a beautiful sight full of stars. A third object, the open cluster IC 2157 can also be found on the other side of M35, but appears fainter than its neighbors.
name: M35

description: Messier 36 is one of the three Messier bright star clusters in the constellation of Auriga, the two others being M37 and M38. M36 is pretty similar to the famous Pleiades cluster (M45), but is much fainter and farther.
name: Pinwheel Cluster

description: There are three open clusters in the constellation of Auriga, M37 being one of them. It is the largest, brightest, and most populated of the three.
name: M37

description: The last Messier cluster in Auriga is M38, also called the Starfish Cluster due to its shape of an X. It was discovered in 1654 by Giovanni Battista Hodierna, although Guillaume Le Gentil discovered it independently in 1749.
name: Starfish Cluster

description: Messier 39 is one of the nearest clusters to Earth, after the Pleiades (M45), the Beehive (M44), and a couple of others.
name: M39

description: M4 is a globular cluster located in Scorpius, west of the star Antares. It concentrates fewer stars than most globular clusters but is known to host many white dwarfs (dense form taken by stars of a size similar to the Sun, after their death).
name: M4

description: M40 (also commonly known as Winnecke 4), is one of the three entries in the Messier catalog that are not considered Deep-Sky Objects. The first one being M24 (The Sagitarrius Star Cloud), and the third being M73, an asterism formed by 4 stars. Messier 40 is simply a double star, which was found when he was trying to spot a nearby galaxy. Charles Messier found the double star instead, as he did not have a big enough telescope to spot the galaxy he was looking for.
name: Double Star M40 (WNC 4)

description: Just next to the brightest star in the entire night sky, Sirius, is the open cluster Messier 41. The cluster is pretty sparse and contains about 100 stars.
name: M41

description:
"M42 is the easiest nebula to find, and is located in Orion’s sword. It lies between other deep-sky objects, such as Messier 78, the Horsehead and Flame nebulae, and even the Witch Head nebula.
Messier 42 is one of the brightest nebulae in the sky, and is easily visible with the unaided eye although it looks just like a regular star."
name: Orion Nebula

description: "Messier 43 (named after its discoverer: Jean-Jacques d'Ortous de Mairan) is an H II region that is visibly part of the Orion Nebula. Both objects are only separated by a lane of dust."
name: De Mairan’s Nebula

description: M44, most often called the Beehive Cluster, is the third brightest object in the Messier catalog, and can be seen with the naked eye. In photographs, the cluster appears mostly white and blue, but it also contains a few red and orange stars.
name: Beehive Cluster

description:
"First observed by Galileo Galilei, Messier 45 is best known as the beautiful Seven Sisters of the night sky! M45, also known as the Pleiades, is an open cluster in the Taurus constellation. The cluster contains about 3,000 stars, equivalent to the world’s tiger population. The stars are about 100 million years old. Because these stars are only loosely bound by gravity, the cluster is expected to disperse in 250 million years. Stars that have not died by then will mix with the other stars of the Milky Way.
The cluster’s blue color is due to the presence of giant, massive stars that are hotter than the Sun and emit more blue light than other light. The haze around this cluster comes from the gas and dust that scatters the blue light of the stars."
name: Pleiades

description: Messier 46 is a 300 million years old open cluster that is home to 500 stars, in the constellation of Puppis. NGC 2438, a planetary nebula, is also seen when observing or photographing M46, it is thought that the nebula is in front of and not behind the cluster from our point of view.
name: M46

description: Visible to the naked eye under perfect dark skies, M47 is a relatively bright open cluster in the constellation of Puppis, not far from Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky. Home to only 50 stars, M47 is one of the least populated clusters known.
name: M47

description: In the largest constellation of the sky, Hydra, is M48, an open cluster of stars, 1,500 light-years away from us. Charles Messier noted that the cluster was at a short distance from the three stars that form the beginning of the Unicorn‘s tail.
name: M48

description: Messier 49 is an elliptical galaxy in Virgo. The galaxy looks yellowish and does not show any details in its gases. M49 is home to about 5,900 globular clusters!
name: M49

description: Satellite of our Milky Way galaxy, the globular cluster M5 is not only one of the largest ones, but with an estimated age of 13 billion years (almost the age of the universe), it is also one of the oldest clusters known!
name: M5

description: To the East of Orion, M50, also called the Heart-Shaped cluster, is an open cluster is Monoceros that appears mostly blue.
name: Heart-Shaped Cluster

description: M51 is a grand-design spiral galaxy which can be found pretty easily in the constellation of Canes Venatici. The Whirlpool galaxy is very famous due to its impressive act of being in the process of swallowing its companion: NGC 5195.
name: Whirlpool Galaxy

description: Messier 52 is an open cluster with a strong central concentration of stars, in the constellation of Cassiopeia.
name: M52

description: M53 is a globular cluster not far from the orange giant Arcturus, the fourth brightest star in our sky. Messier 53 has a very bright core and contains more than 500,000 stars.
name: M53

description: Messier 54 is very easy to find due to its location in the sky near the bright stars of Sagittarius, but it is very difficult to see any details in the cluster. Being an extragalactic globular cluster (from a different galaxy than our Milky Way), M54 will look like a hazy patch of light, even through telescopes. This object is just one of the two Messier objects that are from a different galaxy than ours, the second being M79.
name: M54

description: M55 is a dim globular cluster of stars, that never rises high in the sky for Northern observers.
name: Summer Rose Star

description: Messier 56 is a globular cluster located very close to the only other Messier object in the constellation of Lyra: the Ring nebula (M57).
name: M56

description: M57, or the Ring Nebula, is a planetary nebula similar in shape to the bigger Helix nebula. It is one of the faintest objects in the entire Messier Catalog, but is a very popular target for observers and astrophotographers due to its high surface brightness.
name: Ring Nebula

description: M58 is a barred spiral galaxy that can be found in the Virgo cluster of galaxies. With an apparent magnitude of 10.5, Messier 58 is the brightest member of the Virgo group. It is interesting to note that M58 is the most distant object in the entire Messier catalog!
name: M58

description: In the heart of the Virgo supercluster is the elliptical galaxy Messier 59. M59 is home to a supermassive black hole 100 times more massive than the canter black hole of our Milky Way.
name: M59

description: "The Butterfly cluster is classified as an open cluster. It is located north of the Scorpion's tail and is part of the Milky Way, in direction of the galactic center. The cluster concentrates a hundred stars, mostly young hot blue stars."
name: Butterfly Cluster

description: To the very East of the Virgo cluster of galaxies, is Messier 60, a bright giant elliptical galaxy. Not much can be seen when observing or photographing M60, mostly because its brightness, and the type of galaxy it is makes it appear like a blob of light in the sky.
name: M60

description: Towards the South of the Virgo cluster of galaxies is one of the largest galaxies of the group: the barred spiral galaxy Messier 61. M61 is also classified as a starburst galaxy, as it is forming new stars at a very high speed.
name: M61

description: M62 is a globular cluster, not far from M19. Charles Messier discovered the cluster on June 7, 1771, but did not enter it into his catalog until June 4, 1779, because he noted the wrong coordinates during his original discovery.
name: M62

description:
"M63 is a spiral galaxy located about 37 million light-years away from Earth, it is a member of the M51 group of galaxies.
The Sunflower galaxy got its name from its yellow core and the shape of its arms resembling a sunflower, and is a lot of observers' and astrophotographers' favorite!"
name: Sunflower Galaxy

description: M64, also called the Black Eye galaxy, the Evil Eye galaxy, and the Sleeping Beauty galaxy, is a spiral galaxy lying 24 million light-years away from Earth. Messier 64 is most famous for its dark bands of dust passing in front of its core.
name: Black Eye Galaxy

description: "The Leo Triplet is composed of two Messier objects, M65 and M66, as well as NGC 3628, often called the Hamburger galaxy due to its shape. All three galaxies are getting deformed by each other's gravity, but Messier 65 is the one that is the least affected, and looks like a normal spiral galaxy."
name: M65

description: Messier 66 is part of the Leo Triplet, and is the one to the East of the group. It has been deformed by the gravitational pull of its two neighbors, so much that its core is now not in the center of the galaxy anymore.
name: M66

description: With an age of between 3 and 5 billion years, Messier 67, in the constellation of Cancer, is the oldest open cluster in the entire Messier Catalog. The stars are expected to disperse in about 5 billion years.
name: King Cobra Cluster

description: Messier 68 is a globular cluster in Hydra, and more than 2,000 of its 100,000+ stars are visible from Earth. The cluster is located behind the galactic center and looks like a faint patch of light through binoculars and small instruments.
name: M68

description: Near the core of our galaxy lies a beautiful globular cluster, Messier 69. It is also near M70, another globular from the Messier Catalog.
name: M69

description: M7 is an open cluster located near the sting of Scorpius. It is one of the closest open clusters of our solar system, it approaches it at a speed of 14 km / s. It concentrates a hundred stars, mostly young blue stars. Messier describes it as a cluster of small stars, among which there is one which has more light.
name: "Ptolemy's Cluster"

description: In the Teapot asterism of the Sagittarius constellation is the globular cluster M70. It is the neighbor of two other Messier globulars, M54 and M69. M70 is only 1,800 light-years away from M69.
name: M70

description: Within the famous Summer Triangle lies M71, a globular cluster with a density classification of X, XI. Messier 71 was once thought to be a very populated cluster, such as M11, but it is actually a very loose object.
name: M71

description: "Similar to Messier 4 and Messier 12, M72 is a pretty faint globular cluster, which can be found in the constellation of Aquarius. M72's age is about 9.5 billion years old and is one of the faintest and smallest objects in Charles Messier's catalog."
name: M72

description: "Very close to the globular cluster Messier 72, M73 is an asterism formed by 4 stars. It was the third and last of Messier's mistakes, as M73 is not considered to be a deep-sky object."
name: M73

description: The Phantom Galaxy is a grand design spiral galaxy, with a large apparent size but a low surface brightness.
name: Phantom Galaxy

description: "Messier 75 is a dense globular cluster that can be found in the constellation of Sagittarius. It contains about 400,000 stars and lies 47,600 light-years beyond the Milky Way's galactic center."
name: M75

description: Also named the Cork nebula or the Barbell nebula, M76 is very similar to M27, the Dumbbell nebula, but appears much smaller. The Little Dumbbell nebula is one of the 4 planetary nebulae in the Messier catalog.
name: Little Dumbbell Nebula

description: Large and with a bright core, M77 is a barred spiral galaxy in Cetus. It is the central member of the M77 Group, which contains several bound galaxies.
name: Cetus A

description: M78 is located in the constellation of the Hunter: Orion. Messier 78 is a diffuse reflection nebula, near the Orion nebula, the Horsehead and the Flame nebulae.
name: M78

description: M79 is the second and last extragalactic globular cluster listed in Messier’s catalog, the first one being Messier 54. M79 lies in the constellation of Lepus, and is located in the Canis Major dwarf galaxy, a satellite of ours.
name: M79

description: The Lagoon Nebula is a giant cloud of dust and interstellar gas emitting light in different wavelengths, which explains the richness of its colors (although to the naked eye, it is only visible in gray-green). The nebula is home to bright young stars that give the Lagoon nebula its brilliance, like the giant star Herschel 36, 32 times more massive and 200,000 times brighter than the Sun but hidden by thick clouds of dust.
name: Lagoon Nebula

description: Messier 80 is a globular cluster in the constellation of the Scorpion: Scorpius. It lies just to the northwest of Antares, the brightest star in Scorpius. M80 is not far from another Messier cluster: Messier 4.
name: M80

description: M81 is a grand design spiral galaxy discovered by Johann Elert Bode in 1774. It is the largest object of the M81 group of galaxies, which contains 34 galaxies in Ursa Major.
name: "Bode's Galaxy"

description: In the same field of view as Messier 81 is M82, or the Cigar galaxy, an edge-on starburst galaxy that is about 5 times more luminous than the Milky Way. In 2014, a team of researchers discovered the brightest ever pulsar known inside M82, with a luminosity of 100 times what was thought to be possible.
name: Cigar Galaxy

description: M83 is a barred spiral galaxy in the largest constellation of the night sky: Hydra. The Southern Pinwheel Galaxy is one of the most difficult objects from the Messier catalog to observe because it never rises high above the horizon.
name: Southern Pinwheel Galaxy

description: "Messier 84 is a galaxy in Virgo. It is one of the brightest galaxies of the Virgo cluster, and it is also part of Markarian's Chain."
name: M84

description: Towards the North of the Virgo cluster is M85, a galaxy similar in shape, size and brightness to Messier 84.
name: M85

description: In the same field of view as Messier 84 is another Messier object: M86. It is very similar to its neighbor, and it is also uncertain whether it is an elliptical or a lenticular galaxy.
name: M86

description: Messier 87 is a supergiant elliptical galaxy in Virgo. M87 is also called Virgo A, or even the Smoking Gun due to the jet of gas expelling from its core, visible in photographs. M87 has an impressive total mass of 2.7 trillion solar masses.
name: Virgo A

description: M88 is a beautiful, slightly inclined spiral galaxy that looks like a small, purple Andromeda galaxy.
name: M88

description: Messier 89 is an elliptical galaxy part of the Virgo Cluster. M89 is very round, which is rare for ellipticals, as they often have a slight oval shape.
name: M89

description: Messier 9 is a star cluster located in the southern part of the constellation of Ophiuchus. It is the nearest globular cluster to the galactic center, with a distance of 5,500 light-years. Its age is estimated at 12 billion years, almost as old as the Universe itself. The cluster concentrates many of the oldest stars of the Universe, 13 variable stars and many red giants (the destiny of our Sun at the end of its life).
name: M9

description: M90 is a spiral galaxy, near several other Messier objects where the Virgo cluster is located. Messier 90 is in the process of slowly turning into a lenticular galaxy.
name: M90

description: Messier 91 is one of the most difficult Messier objects to observe in the night sky, because of its magnitude and size. Photographing the galaxy will allow you to see the bar that makes it a barred spiral galaxy, but it is extremely difficult to see it visually.
name: M91

description: M92 is a globular cluster, similar to the famous Hercules Globular Cluster (M13) but smaller and fainter. Both clusters also lie in the same constellation.
name: M92

description: Near Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is an open cluster, Messier 93. The cluster contains hundreds of stars, although only about 80 were confirmed.
name: M93

description: "Messier 94 is a beautiful spiral galaxy, that has the shape of a feline's eye. M94 is part of the Canes Venatici I Cloud, which is home to about 20 galaxies, including the Black Eye galaxy. Messier 94 is the brightest one of the group."
name: Cat’s Eye Galaxy

description: Messier 95 is a barred spiral galaxy that is part of the M96 galaxy group (also known as the Leo I Group). M95 has a magnitude of 11.4, and is simply impossible to spot with the naked eye. It is also extremely difficult to see with binoculars.
name: M95

description:
"M96 is considered an intermediate spiral galaxy, and just like M95, it is part of the Leo I Group of galaxies. The group is made up of more than 12 galaxies, including three Messier objects.
Astronomers found that there was a greater concentration of dust in the right side of the galaxy, and deducted that the right side of M96 was closer to Earth than the left."
name: M96

description: Messier 97 is found in the constellation of Ursa Major just under the bright star Merak. The Owl nebula is a very small, faint, and unimpressive object, but it is a popular target for astrophotographers. The main reason being it lies near the Surfboard galaxy, or M108.
name: Owl Nebula

description: M98 is an intermediate spiral galaxy that is part of the Virgo Cluster. It has a very low surface brightness and is one of the faintest objects in the Messier catalog, making it a difficult target to observe.
name: M98

description: Messier 99, or the Coma Pinwheel galaxy, is a member of the large Virgo Cluster. The galaxy has an asymmetric shape similar to M101, the regular Pinwheel galaxy.
name: Coma Pinwheel

description: Mars is the 4th planet orbiting our Sun, and it is most likely the next place where humans will set foot! Mars is a rocky planet with about one-third the gravity of Earth. One day on the planet is just a little over 24 hours, but one year is much longer than an on Earth, with 687 days!
name: Mars

description:
"The Hyades, also known as Melotte 25, is an open cluster located in the constellation Taurus. The name of the cluster comes from the Rain Nymphs, daughter of Atlas and half-sister of the Pleiades. It is the closest open cluster to us with an estimated distance of only 150 light years. It contains at least 515 stars and is about 800 million years old. When the cluster was formed its total mass must have been about 1,500 times the mass of the Sun. But since then, the cluster has lost mass. Some of the most massive stars have died, the mass has been dispersed by dynamical interactions and some stars are regularly ejected from the cluster. Among the remaining stars, the most massive are about 2.5 times heavier than the Sun. We also note the presence of some white dwarfs, a residual type of star, as the Sun will become.
The cluster has a size in the sky of 5°. Mosaic mode is recommended for this observation."
name: Hyades

description:
"The Coma Star Cluster, known as Melotte 111 or Collinder 256, is an open cluster in the Coma Berenices constellation. It should not be confused with the Coma Cluster (Abell 1656), which is a cluster of galaxies also found in the Coma Berenices constellation.
At an estimated distance of only 280 light-years, the open cluster is the second closest open cluster to us after Hyades. The cluster formed about 600 million years ago and studies have currently identified more than 330 members."
name: Coma Star Cluster

description: "Mercury is the smallest and closest planet to the Sun in our Solar System, and if you were to walk on its rocky surface, the sun would look three times bigger than the way we see it on Earth. Two missions were sent to Mercury, Mariner 10 in 1974 and Messenger, which went into the planet's orbit in 2011."
name: Mercury

description:
"Mira is a star in the constellation of the Whale. Its Latin name was given by the astronomer Johannes Hevelius in 1662. It means the wonderful or the surprising. This is because Mira A has the specific characteristic of being a variable star, its brightness can vary up to 8 magnitudes over a period of 333 days even though the cycle is irregular. To the naked eye, the star appears red and very bright before disappearing in the most extreme cases.
However, using more sophisticated instruments, astronomers have discovered that the star is a binary system consisting of a red giant star (Mira A) and a white dwarf (Mira B). The variation of luminosity observed is only related to Mira A.
The origin of this variability is due to regular charging of the properties inside the star. With its advanced age, the heart of the star is composed of carbon and oxygen which does not burn and therefore no longer produces photons. Above this core there is a small shell of burning helium and above this, a shell of burning hydrogen. These nuclear reactions produce photons that make the star grow. As it grows, the luminosity of the star decreases. The temperature also drops and the nuclear reactions stop. Without these reactions, the star contracts, the luminosity increases, the temperature also increases and the reactions start again, creating a new cycle."
name: Mira

description: "The Moon is our planet's only permanent natural satellite, and was formed 4.51 billion years ago. From Earth, we can only see the same side of the Moon because it is in synchronous rotation with our planet. Our satellite makes a full orbit around Earth in 29.5 days."
name: Moon

description:
"Mu Cephei, also known as Herschel's Garnet Star or Erakis, is a red supergiant star in the constellation Cepheus. It is located on the edge of the Elephant’s Trunk nebula, which will give a red color to a portion of the background sky in the image. This red-looking star in the sky, as noted by astronomer William Herschel, has a surface temperature of 3,475°C. This is more than twice the temperature needed to melt cast iron. Its radius is estimated to be about 1,200 times that of our Sun, making it one of the 15 largest stars known. If we replaced the Sun with this star, its surface would be located between the orbit of Jupiter and Saturn.
Weighing 25 times the mass of the Sun at birth, the star loses the equivalent of the mass of the Earth each year. Having burned the hydrogen in its core, the current temperature of over 100 million degrees is now high enough for the helium to fuse and transform into carbon. The hydrogen in the layers surrounding the nucleus is transformed into helium."
name: "Herschel's Garnet Star"

description: "Napoleon's Hat, also known as Picot 1, is an asterism in the Bootes constellation. The group of stars near Arcturus resembles the famous “bicorne” (two-pointed hat) of the emperor of the French Napoleon. The asterism was discovered in 1995 by the amateur astronomer Fulbert Picot."
name: "Napoleon's Hat"

description: Neptune is an ice giant, and the 8th planet from the Sun. It has 13 moons, named after sea gods and nymphs from the Greek mythology. The planet also has 6 confirmed rings. Just like Uranus, the planet was never studied from up close, and Voyager 2 was the only spacecraft to ever fly by it.
name: Neptune

description: NGC 1023, also known as the Perseus Lenticular Galaxy, is, as its name suggests, a lenticular-type galaxy in the Perseus constellation. It has a diameter of 57,000 light-years, in other words, nearly half the size of the Milky Way. Its center contains a supermassive black hole of 44 million solar masses. The galaxy has almost already consumed all of its gas and can no longer form new stars. The stars are actually mostly old, which gives the image a yellow-orange color. On the disk, note the presence of rare young clusters with blue stars.
name: Perseus Lenticular Galaxy

description: With an apparent size similar to the full moon, 47 Tucanae is the second largest, but also brightest globular cluster in the night sky. In May 2015, researchers showed the first evidence of dynamic mass segregation happening inside the globular cluster.
name: 47 Tucanae

description: Located in Cetus, about 45 million light-years from the Milky Way, NGC 1055 is a barred spiral galaxy seen from the edge. Reminiscent of the most famed Sombrero galaxy, it is distinguished by its central bulb and its very marked dust lanes, dense obscuring bands of interstellar dust.
name: NGC 1055

description: NGC 1073 is a barred spiral galaxy located in Cetus, the fourth largest constellation in the sky. It is part of a group of 7 galaxies (including M77 and NGC 1055) whose average distance from the Milky Way is estimated at 55 million light-years.
name: NGC 1073

description:
"NGC 1097, also known as Caldwell 67, is a spiral galaxy in the Fornax constellation.
The central black hole at the heart of this galaxy weighs 140 million solar masses. Stretching out from the central bulge is a bar-like structure from which two spiral arms emerge. The spiral arms are considerably distorted by interactions with a satellite galaxy. Matter from the outer part is attracted toward the inner parts of the galaxy creating a ring 5,000 light-years from the center. This area is conducive to new star formation."
name: NGC 1097

description:
"NGC 1232 is a spiral galaxy in the Eridanus constellation.
From a virtually face-on view, it presents well defined spiral arms that are illuminated by numerous stars. In the central areas, the old stars emit the yellow-orange color, while in the outer areas, the young stars emit the blue colors. Its size is between that of our galaxy and that of Andromeda.
Slightly detached from the arms, note the presence of a small diffuse luminous spot. It is a satellite galaxy of NGC 1232."
name: NGC 1232

description: NGC 1245 is an open cluster in the Perseus constellation. According to Gaia Mission results, the cluster contains at least 479 1.2-billion-year-old stars in a sphere less than 40 light-years in diameter. Comparatively, within a radius of 20 light-years around the Sun, there are less than 100 known stars. The cluster also contains 5 blue straggler stars, which are warmer and brighter than the rest of their companions. They are not cluster members but rather foreground stars. The whole thing is approaching us at 30 km/s. The two bright stars in the middle of the image however are HD 20023 and HD 20077.
name: NGC 1245

description:
"Situated just 230 million light-years away, NGC 1275, also known as Perseus A, lies tucked away within the sprawling northern Perseus constellation.
This stellar island ranks among the nearest giant elliptical galaxies and most powerful source of steady radio emissions in the entire sky.
Appearing as a condensed snowball with circular halos through telescopes, this cosmic titan, spans some 100,000 light years across and also happens to be the brightest member within a massive collection of galaxies called the Perseus cluster.
NGC 1275 lies at the center of this cluster some 275 million light years away. The cluster is considered one of the most massive objects in the Universe containing thousands of galaxies within a diameter of about 12 million light years."
name: Perseus A

description:
"NGC 1313 is a barred spiral galaxy visible in Reticulum, a faint constellation in the southern sky. This active galaxy is part of the starburst galaxy classification as indicated by its huge amount of oxygen-rich nebulae and its massive young stars population. 
 
The heterogeneous or the asymmetric spiral arms visible in NGC 1313 suggest a past chaotic milestone; for example a potential collision with another galaxy. This hypothesis is still under scrutiny. One main source of doubt is that as NGC 1313 is a field galaxy; therefore it is wandering in the interstellar medium and gravitational interaction with other galaxies is unlikely."
name: Topsy Turvy Galaxy

description: The Fornax Cluster, also known as ACO S373, is a cluster of galaxies primarily located in the Fornax constellation with partial spillover into the Eridanus. It is the second richest cluster of galaxies within 100 million light-years of us. The cluster contains more than 500 galaxies with a total mass of 70,000 billion times the mass of the Sun. It is divided into two subgroups centered on the elliptical galaxy NGC 1399 for the first, and on the lenticular galaxy NGC 1316, for the second. NGC 1316 is also the biggest and brightest galaxy in the group. On the image, centered on NGC 1316, a significant portion of the yellow-orange points are not stars, they are galaxies
name: Fornax Cluster (NGC 1316)

description: The Robin’s Egg Nebula, also known as NGC 1360, is a planetary nebula in the Fornax constellation. 10,000 years ago, a dying star created this nebula that expanded into the interstellar medium. Its current shape resembles a rugby ball the size of which is about 3 light-years in length. The material of the nebula has begun to merge and mix with the interstellar medium. The blue color in the image is caused by the presence of oxygen in the nebula. Being heated by the remnant star, it emits light in this band of color. The central star is a system consisting of two white dwarfs. The mass of each of the stars is estimated to be ⅔ that of the current Sun and their temperature over 100,000°C.
name: "Robin's Egg Nebula"

description: NGC 1365 is a double-barred spiral galaxy that can be found in the constellation Fornax. It is located 56 millions light-years away and has a magnitude of 9,6. Due to its shape, it is also called The Great Spiral Galaxy.
name: Great Barred Spiral Galaxy

description: The Fornax Cluster, also known as ACO S373, is a cluster of galaxies primarily located in the Fornax constellation with partial spillover into the Eridanus. It is the second richest cluster of galaxies within 100 million years of us. The cluster contains more than 500 galaxies with a total mass of 70,000 billion times the mass of the Sun. It is divided into two subgroups centered on the elliptical galaxy NGC 1399 for the first, and on the lenticular galaxy NGC 1316, for the second. NGC 1316 is also the biggest and brightest galaxy in the group. On the image, centered on NGC 1399, a significant portion of the yellow-orange points are not stars, they are galaxies
name: Fornax Cluster (NGC 1399)

description: NGC 147, also known as Caldwell 17, is a dwarf galaxy in the Cassiopeia constellation. The galaxy resembles an American football with a length of 11,000 light-years and a width of 7,500 light-years. The total mass of the galaxy is estimated to be 55 million times that of the Sun. The galaxy is in fact a satellite of the Andromeda Galaxy M31. The stars in the galaxy formed more than 3 billion years ago. There seems to be no gas left in the galaxy and the interstellar medium is empty. The galaxy can no longer form new stars.
name: NGC 147

description: NGC 1491, also known as SH 2-206, is an emission nebula in the Perseus constellation. Unlike many emission nebulae, this region of gas and dust is not heated by a nearby open cluster but by a single star. Named BD +50° 886, it is a massive star that represents 40 solar masses. Its surface temperature is 45,000°C. Its luminosity is 350,000 times that of our star. The matter expelled from the star will accelerate to several hundred km/s and ram and compress the gas in the interstellar medium that surrounds it. The photons emitted by the star will heat the interstellar medium.
name: SH 2-206

description: The California nebula is an emission nebula from the Perseus constellation. It is only 1000 light-years away, located in the Orion Arm, a minor spiral arm of the Milky Way galaxy. Of an apparent magnitude of 6, its red color reflects a strong presence of hydrogen.
name: California Nebula

description: "Kemble's Cascade is a famous asterism visible in the constellation of the Giraffe: Camelopardalis. It was named in honor of Lucien Kemble, who wrote about the asterism as a beautiful cascade of stars."
name: "Kemble's Cascade"

description:
"NGC 1555, also referred to as Hind's Variable Nebula, Sh2-238, or HH 155, is a dynamic nebula 400 light years from Earth, nestled within the borders of Taurus, the bull constellation.
The discovery of this nebula dates back to October 11, 1852, credited to the keen eye of John Russell Hind. As its name suggests this 4 light year diameter gas cloud actually changes its shape and brightness thanks to the nearby variable star called T Tauri that is embedded in dust and gas. But T Tauri is actually composed of three, very young individual stars very close together, with one believed to still be at its earliest stages of formation."
name: "Hind's Variable Nebula"

description: NGC 1579 is a diffuse nebula in the Perseus Constellation, also called the Northern Trifid because of its similarity to M20. The color of this region of ionized hydrogen, known as the HII region (as in H2), is mainly due to its gas being excited by radiation from the star LkHα 101. This 15 solar mass star is part of a young cluster, about 1 million years old, in which stars are still forming. In addition to LkH α 101, 5 other stars larger than 10 solar masses have been detected.
name: Northern Trifid
